html.body: REM1499455565,6125212016-08-182016-08-18REM DOCUMENTApplication No.: 14/994,555Attorney Docket No.: 11541-0039-01000REMARKSApplicant submits this Reply in response to the Office Action mailed on May 18, 2016.Status of the Claims Claims 1-20 are currently pending in this application. By this Amendment, Applicant amends claims 1, 3, 6, 8, 9, 11, 17, and 19. The originally filed specification and drawings fully support the subject matter of the amended claims, for example, at paragraphs [0022] and [0029]. Applicant believes that this Amendment adds no new matter.Applicant respectfully requests the Examiner's reconsideration and withdrawal of the pending rejections for at least the reasons that follow.Specification The Examiner objects to paragraph [0037] of the disclosure stating that OD simulated flow is not clear. However, paragraph [0037] of the disclosure states, "step 227 may include performing a 3D, 1D, or OD (e.g., reduced order model) fluid simulation of blood flow in the modeled vasculature of at least the identified area of interest of the patient-specific model."Applicant respectfully submits that those of skill in the art appreciate that a "OD" model is a "zero-D" or "zero-dimensional" model. A zero-D or OD model may include a "reduced order model," as described above and in Applicant's originally filed specification. A zero-D or OD model may also include a "lumped parameter" model, as would be appreciated by one of skill in the art. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully-12-Application No.: 14/994,555Attorney Docket No.: 11541-0039-01000submits that the definition of a OD model for simulated flow is clear. Reconsideration of this specification objection is requested.Claim Objections The Office Action objected to claims 6 and 8 for allegedly having minor informalities. (Office Action, page 2.) This objection is rendered moot by Applicant's claim amendments to claims 6 and 8. Applicant requests that the claim objections be withdrawn.Section 112 RejectionsClaims 3, 4, 6-8, 11, 12, and 14-16 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(pre-AIA) (first paragraph) as allegedly failing to comply with the enablement requirement for the claim feature of, "determining blood flow demand based on a received physiological state and the portion of the patient's bowel." The Office Action reasons that the Specification fails to teach the claim feature on the basis that paragraph [0035] of the original specification teaches, "blood flow demand may be calculated based on an allometric relationship between total blood flow and tissue mass, e.g., resting flow (QR) is proportional to mass', where # may be an empirically derived constant (e.g., in the 2- 3 range)." Specifically, the Office Action states, "this is not blood flow demand based upon any physiological requirement, but rather appears to be a baseline (resting) mean blood flow," and the Office Action further states, "the determination using a physiological state and a portion of a patient's bowel is inconsistent with the previously defined allometric relationship between total blood flow and tissue mass. Accordingly, the claimed invention is non-enabled." (Office Action, pages 4-6.)-13-Application No.: 14/994,555Attorney Docket No.: 11541-0039-01000Accounting for the physiological state in determining a blood flow demand may permit a more refined determination of the blood flow demand. Paragraph [0029] of the original specification states, "[f]or example, a patient's tissue may have higher blood flow demand during an exercise state, than during a patient's resting state. Accounting for physiological state in determining a blood flow characteristic may provide greater context or accuracy in the resultant determined blood flow characteristic." Thus, "determining blood flow demand based on a received physiological state and the portion of the patient's bowel" may be an enhancement of a blood flow demand possibly found via an allometric relationship. The claim feature is not at odds with the defined allometric relationship.The Office Action also states, "the determination of blood flow demand being inferred from a patient's liver mass is non-enabled and would require undue experimentation to determine." However, the currently-amended independent claims recite, "determining a tissue region of the patient's bowel distal to the location in the patient-specific anatomic model of the patient's visceral vasculature; [and] determining a blood flow demand of the determined tissue region." (Emphasis added.) The claims do not recite determining blood flow demand from a patient's liver mass.Applicant thus requests the Examiner's reconsideration and withdrawal of theSection 112 rejections.Section 103 RejectionsApplicant respectfully traverses the rejection of claims 1-20, which were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Taylor (U.S. Publication No. 2012/0041318 Al) ("Taylor') in view of T. Mabotuwana, L. Cheng, and A Pullan ("-14-Application No.: 14/994,555Attorney Docket No.: 11541-0039-01000A model of blood flow in the mesenteric arterial system" Biomed Eng Onlin. 2007) ("Mabotuwana").To expedite prosecution, Applicant amends the claims to recite, "determining a blood flow demand of the determined tissue region; . . . and generating an assessment of blood supply adequacy defining an adequacy of blood supply to the tissue region of the patient's viscera or bowel based on the determined blood flow characteristic, or generating a risk score defining a risk of disease of the patient's viscera or bowel, based on the determined blood flow characteristic and an expected blood flow characteristic associated with the tissue region of the patient's bowel based on the determined blood flow characteristic." (Emphasis added.)Neither Taylor nor Mabotuwana, individually or in combination, would have rendered obvious the above-recited subject matter.For the reasons discussed, Applicant submits that claims 1-20 are allowable over all of the cited references. Accordingly, Applicant requests the Examiner's reconsideration and withdrawal of the Section 103 rejections.ConclusionThe Office Action contains characterization of the claims and the related art with which the Applicant does not necessarily agree. Unless expressly noted otherwise, Applicant declines to subscribe to any statement or characterization in the Office Action.In discussing the specification, claims, and drawings in this Reply, it is to be understood that Applicant is in no way intending to limit the scope of the claims to any exemplary embodiments described in the specification or abstract and/or shown in the-15-Application No.: 14/994,555Attorney Docket No.: 11541-0039-01000drawings. Rather, Applicant is entitled to have the claims interpreted broadly to the maximum extent permitted by statute, regulation, and applicable case law.In view of the foregoing remarks, Applicant submits that this claimed invention is neither anticipated nor rendered obvious in view of the prior art references cited against this application. Applicant therefore requests the reconsideration and reexamination of the application, and the timely allowance of the pending claims.If the Examiner believes a telephone conversation might advance prosecution, the Examiner is invited to call applicant's undersigned representative at 202-803-8075.Please grant any extensions of time required to enter this response and charge any additional required fees to Deposit Account No. 50-5906. In addition, the Commissioner is hereby authorized to charge any additional fees due and any other fees due under 37 C.F.R. § 1.16 or § 1.17 during the pendency of this application to Deposit Account No. 50-5906.Respectfully submitted, BOOKOFF McANDREWS, PLLCCustomer Number: 108,449Dated: August 18, 2016 By: SVG14994555.08-18-2016.IS0RHJWWRXEAPX3.REM.5.19.1272.2173.2015.2219.svg0.1532.477Chemistry Lian HuangReg.
